surveyDefinition.title: Video Streaming Subscriptions — consumer survey (Asia Pacific)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Video Streaming Subscriptions. Every question asks about Video Streaming Subscriptions specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Asia Pacific actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Asia Pacific who buy or use Video Streaming Subscriptions for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Currently has an active paid subscription to at least one video streaming service (e.g., Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max, etc.); Primary decision-maker or co-decision-maker for household streaming subscriptions; Aged 18 or older; Able to complete an online survey in the relevant language. Excluded: Individuals who only use free ad-supported streaming (e.g., free tier of Pluto TV, YouTube without subscription); Businesses or institutions purchasing streaming for commercial use (e.g., bars, hotels, offices); Cable/satellite TV subscribers who do not also have a streaming subscription; Children under 18 (unless surveyed via parent proxy, which is out of scope for this consumer survey).
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Video streaming subscriptions are purchased by individual consumers and households for personal entertainment use. While some business plans exist, the dominant and defining market is consumer subscription services (e.g., Netflix, Disney+, Hulu).
respondentBehaviours: Streams video content at least weekly
Subscribes to one or more paid streaming services
Engages with original content and on-demand viewing
May churn or rotate subscriptions based on content library
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with video streaming and their viewing context, then moves into how they discover, subscribe, and pay for services, including their spending and decision drivers. It then explores their preferences and expectations for features, quality, and value, and finally assesses satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, and future intent. The arc is designed to be progressive: from broad and neutral to specific and sensitive, with money and satisfaction judgments placed late in their sections.

metadata.storyline_summary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with video streaming and their viewing context, then moves into how they discover, subscribe, and pay for services, including their spending and decision drivers. It then explores their preferences and expectations for features, quality, and value, and finally assesses satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, and future intent. The arc is designed to be progressive: from broad and neutral to specific and sensitive, with money and satisfaction judgments placed late in their sections.
storyline_notes: Adapted the canonical arc for a subscription service: replaced 'restock' with 'subscription cycle and rotation' to capture churn and rotation behavior common in streaming.
Added a beat on 'subscription channels' to reflect the importance of local payment methods and telecom bundles in Asia Pacific.

In consumer_profile, merged 'usage occasion' and 'household role' into distinct beats but added 'content needs and motivations' to capture the strong regional language and cultural content drivers in the region.
In preferences_expectations, added 'content format preferences' to capture the importance of regional language content, live sports, and original content in Asia Pacific.
In satisfaction_future_intent, kept the canonical order but emphasized switching triggers and future use to reflect the high churn and rotation behavior in the region.
No brand names or competitor names are used; all questions are category-level.
metadata.classification_reason: Video streaming subscriptions are purchased by individual consumers and households for personal entertainment use. While some business plans exist, the dominant and defining market is consumer subscription services (e.g., Netflix, Disney+, Hulu).
